key_insight: An LLM-powered “sighted guide” can meaningfully support blind and low vision (BLV) users to navigate and ask questions in social VR, but its usefulness depends on social context, accuracy, and trust-related concerns uncovered in a 16-participant study.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of practical, user-evaluated solutions for making social VR navigation and in-situ information access accessible to BLV people.
method: Built an LLM-powered guide agent that provides navigation help and answers user queries inside social VR environments.
Conducted a mixed-methods user study with 16 BLV participants interacting in VR while confederates posed as other users to simulate social scenarios.
Collected behavioral data and qualitative feedback to evaluate usability, perceived usefulness, trust, and social acceptability.
impact: Provides concrete evidence and design lessons for deploying LLM agents in accessibility-sensitive, social VR settings — highlighting the need to handle accuracy, personalization, multimodal cues, and social dynamics when building accessible AI features.
visual_elements: System diagram: LLM guide pipeline showing input (user speech/commands), LLM processing, and VR output (audio cues/annotations).
Study flow schematic: participant in VR, confederates, scenarios tested, and measures collected (usability, trust, accuracy).
Summary chart: qualitative themes or a small bar chart of participant-reported usefulness vs. concerns (accuracy, privacy, social comfort).
Icon set: BLV user, headset, chat/LLM bubble, and trust/privacy shield to convey core topics quickly.
paper_title: Understanding the Use of a Large Language Model-Powered Guide to Make Virtual Reality Accessible for Blind and Low Vision People
paper_authors: Jazmin Collins, Sharon Y Lin, Tianqi Liu, Andrea Stevenson Won, Shiri Azenkot
